title: Dolphins, Mooring Dolphins and Berthing Dolphins
analyses: Berthing impact and energy absorption analysis
Mooring load and line force analysis
Pile lateral and axial capacity analysis
Wave, current and vessel-induced loading analysis

models.text: The suite should implement static equilibrium, elastic beam bending, Timoshenko shear deformation, beam-column theory, Euler buckling, matrix stiffness formulations, nonlinear frame analysis, vessel kinetic energy models, conservation of linear momentum, impact energy absorption and nonlinear structural contact mechanics.

The principal methods should include effective berthing mass calculations, added mass correction methods, vessel approach eccentricity factors, nonlinear fender compression models, hyperelastic rubber constitutive models, viscoelastic energy dissipation, fender hysteresis, rate-dependent fender behaviour, nonlinear load–displacement curves and energy-based impact assessment. For high-fidelity vessel contact simulation, nonlinear finite-element contact models and coupled vessel motion–fender response should be included.

The suite should employ catenary line equations, elastic mooring line formulations, quasi-static mooring analysis, dynamic line equations, Morison loading, Airy and Stokes wave theories, current drag models, wind loading and vessel-induced dynamic loading.

The suite should include Winkler beam-on-elastic-foundation theory, p–y lateral soil resistance curves, t–z shaft resistance relationships, q–z pile toe resistance relationships, nonlinear pile-group effects, soil stiffness degradation, cyclic p–y models, lateral pile capacity methods and three-dimensional soil finite-element analysis.

Applicable methods include modal vibration analysis, Rayleigh damping, transient dynamic simulation, S–N fatigue relationships, Palmgren–Miner cumulative damage, rainflow counting, impact-cycle fatigue, seismic response spectrum analysis, nonlinear time-history analysis and residual strength assessment.

The suite should integrate nonlinear vessel approach dynamics, rate-dependent fender behaviour, pile–soil interaction, structural response and probabilistic berthing conditions. Hybrid finite-element and empirical fender models, CFD-derived vessel loading, fatigue damage forecasting and reliability-based collision assessment are appropriate when supported by measured equipment performance and site-specific operating data.

Berthing frequency, repeated impacts, cyclic mooring loads and storm loading statistics.
Abnormal berthing velocities, overloaded mooring lines, collision energy, earthquakes and extreme storms.
Pile corrosion measurements, connection defects, weld inspection findings and observed fender deterioration.

subtitle: Berthing impact, mooring forces, piles, fenders, cyclic loading and structural integrity.
ic: The initial conditions shall define the installed geometry and structural condition of the dolphin, including piles, pile cap, bracing, bollards, fenders and connection components. The structure shall begin from a specified equilibrium state under permanent dead loads, hydrostatic effects and sustained equipment loading.

The initial pile and soil state shall include pile embedment, soil stress, axial and lateral soil resistance, pile-head stiffness and any existing foundation deformation. For existing dolphins, the model shall include observed corrosion, pile damage, fender deterioration and residual deflections where applicable.

Berthing simulations shall begin with the vessel at a defined position, orientation and approach velocity relative to the dolphin. The initial fender compression shall generally be zero when the simulation begins before contact. Mooring analyses shall establish the initial vessel position, line pretension and dolphin load state.

Repeated-impact fatigue simulations shall begin with a specified accumulated damage state or an undamaged reference state. Dynamic simulations shall use initial structural displacement and velocity conditions consistent with the selected starting configuration.
bc: Pile foundations shall be restrained through soil–pile interaction, including axial resistance, lateral resistance, bending restraint and possible nonlinear soil response. Pile-head connections shall represent actual structural continuity with the pile cap.

Fender contact boundaries shall impose vessel impact through appropriate contact and energy-absorption characteristics. Mooring boundaries shall apply line tensions at bollard or hook locations, including the correct load orientations and elevations.

Environmental boundaries shall apply waves, currents, water levels and vessel-induced hydrodynamic loading. Wind-induced vessel loads shall be transmitted through the mooring or berthing interaction where appropriate.

For repeated impacts, cyclic contact forces shall be imposed according to the operating scenario. Earthquake analysis shall introduce ground acceleration at the foundation boundaries. Extreme loading analysis shall permit nonlinear structural response, contact changes, foundation deformation and material yielding where justified by the physical problem.

calibration: Calibration should use physical fender compression tests, full-scale berth impact measurements, instrumented mooring systems, pile lateral load tests and structural vibration measurements.
Fender stiffness, energy absorption, hysteresis and rate-dependent characteristics should be calibrated from manufacturer-certified testing and independent laboratory evidence where available.

Berthing impact parameters should be adjusted using measured vessel approach speeds, contact locations, berthing angles and impact response. Calibration should account for vessel approach conditions and the effective dynamic mass characteristics used by the selected model.
Mooring models should be calibrated using measured line tensions, vessel movements and environmental loading.
Pile–soil interaction should be calibrated against site-specific geotechnical measurements, lateral pile tests, soil stiffness measurements and cyclic pile response records.
Dolphin structural stiffness and damping should be calibrated using controlled load tests, accelerometer measurements and operational modal analysis.
Fatigue and repeated-impact behaviour should be informed by material fatigue experiments, structural connection tests and inspection histories.
verification: Verification should include analytical benchmarks for pile-supported structures, cantilever pile behaviour, lateral loading, beam bending and combined axial-bending response.
Fender compression and energy absorption calculations should be verified against prescribed force-deflection test curves.
Berthing impact calculations should undergo momentum and energy consistency checks appropriate to the selected physical model.
Mooring load resolution should be tested using known line geometries, tensions and fairlead positions.
Pile–soil calculations should undergo benchmark comparisons and mesh or discretization refinement studies.
Dynamic response analyses should be checked through modal benchmarks, time-step convergence and damping sensitivity.
Nonlinear impact simulations should be verified using contact benchmarks, load-increment checks and energy-balance diagnostics.
Fatigue accumulation and failure assessment calculations should be tested against known reference datasets.
validation: Fender reaction and deformation predictions should be compared with independent physical fender tests and recorded real berthing events.
Dolphin displacement and pile response should be assessed using full-scale structural load tests and instrumented berthing events.
Mooring forces should be validated against measured bollard loads and line tensions.
Pile load distribution and foundation deflection predictions should be evaluated against field pile tests and measured dolphin movement.
Repeated impact fatigue predictions should be compared with laboratory cyclic tests and observed deterioration of operating dolphin structures.
Extreme environmental and seismic predictions should be assessed using appropriate physical-model data or documented field events where sufficient measurements exist.
The validation programme should cover the relevant vessel classes, fender types, pile configurations and soil conditions rather than assuming that one berth configuration represents all dolphins.

geometry.text: Single-pile dolphins, multi-pile dolphins, pile caps, braced structures, fender systems, mooring platforms, bollards, quick-release-hook supports and berthing impact structures.

geometry.cat: Conventional and universal CAD geometry formats
geometry.text: STEP, IGES, Parasolid, ACIS, IFC, DXF and supported DWG should be accepted for tubular piles, structural bracing, pile caps, mooring equipment foundations, fender attachments and structural connections.

SDNF, CIS/2, IFC structural representations and suitable CSV, XML or JSON node/member descriptions should be accepted for pile arrangements, structural member connectivity, pile inclination, pile-cap geometry and support conditions. Marine vessel contact geometry can be imported through STEP, IGES, Parasolid or triangulated hull surfaces, provided the contact representation is suitable for the selected analysis.

Nastran BDF, Abaqus INP, ANSYS CDB, Gmsh MSH, UNV, MED, VTK/VTU and Exodus should be supported for pile deformation, fender contact, nonlinear pile–soil interaction, structural fatigue and localized impact analyses.

STL, OBJ, PLY, GLB, E57, LAS/LAZ, XYZ, GeoTIFF and bathymetric surfaces should be accepted for surveyed dolphins, vessel contact zones, marine growth reconstruction, damaged structures and irregular seabed conditions.
